title: torch.compile fails or underperforms for GNN training with NeighborLoader dynamic batches
body: I am training a simple GCN with PyG NeighborLoader, so every mini-batch has dynamic node and edge shapes. Simple gather/scatter compile tests pass, but on my end-to-end NeighborSampling benchmark eager mode is faster than torch.compile, and the logs repeatedly hit Dynamo's cache-size limit because tensor sizes and strides change between batches. This is on an A100 system with a PyTorch 1.14 development build, CUDA 12.0, and the benchmark script and full logs linked.

symptoms_visible: My NeighborLoader GCN takes about 0.84 seconds per epoch in eager mode, while torch.compile repeatedly recompiles for changing node and edge shapes and is slower.
N0.label: N0 dynamic GNN compile performance reported

symptoms_visible: The compiled training benchmark is still slower than eager and uses the older Triton backend from our February container.
N1.label: N1 training mode and old Triton established

symptoms_visible: After building the suggested PR branch, the compiled model exits with a segmentation fault while the eager epoch completes.
N1_x.label: N1_x PR branch on old Triton aftermath

symptoms_visible: With the newer Triton source build and dynamic=True, training raises an error because size() receives a SymInt dimension instead of an int.
N2.label: N2 symbolic dimension failure reproduced

symptoms_visible: With the specialize_int_float patch and the suggested PR branch, the forward pass gets farther but loss.backward() fails with "'int' object has no attribute '_has_symbolic_sizes_strides'".
N2_x.label: N2_x integer-specialization hack aftermath

symptoms_visible: On the latest PyTorch, Triton, PyG, and pyg-lib, Inductor completes training but reports that split reduction could not be used for dynamic shapes; eager is about 0.83 seconds per epoch and compiled is about 1.08 seconds.
N3.label: N3 correctness restored but performance still poor

symptoms_visible: I rebuilt on the current stack and the NeighborLoader training loop now runs to completion with dynamic compilation; I haven't re-timed it yet.
N4.label: N4 reporter verifies dynamic training speedup (fix applied, unverified)

symptoms_visible: The NeighborLoader GCN trains successfully with dynamic compilation and the measured compiled run is about 20% faster than eager.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved

question_patterns: Is this compiling training, including backward, or inference only?
Are you using the old Triton backend or the newer MLIR-based backend, and how was Triton installed?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: This is training, including loss.backward(). I wasn't initially sure how to identify the backend, but our February container builds the Triton commit pinned by PyTorch, and after checking with a colleague I confirmed that it is still the old Triton backend.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: This is inference only with fixed tensor shapes and the current MLIR Triton backend.
It is the same training workload and old backend, installed from a wheel instead of building the pinned source.

edges.comment: The reporter confirmed that the benchmark includes backward and later established that the February container used the old Triton backend.

solution.intent: Patch in PyTorch PR 93059 and rebuild PyTorch, without first changing the container's old Triton backend.
solution.concrete_example: Build PyTorch from the PR 93059 branch and rerun the compiled training benchmark.

edges.comment: Actual failed attempt: the reporter built the suggested PR branch while still using the old backend, and the compiled run segfaulted.

question_patterns: Can you rebuild with the newer Triton backend, set torch.compile(..., dynamic=True), and paste the resulting error?
Please rerun the updated script with dynamic=True and current Triton source.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I rebuilt from the PR branch, installed the latest Triton source, and updated the shared script to call torch.compile with dynamic=True. It still fails. The traceback says size() received an invalid combination of arguments because it got a SymInt, with the failing fake tensor size shown as (s0, s1) and the requested dimension as -2.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: With the new Triton backend and dynamic=True, the full training loop completes and no recompilation or symbolic-size errors appear.
The same SymInt size() error occurs at a different PyG call site in the same training loop.

edges.comment: Handler-initiated backend and configuration probe. The answer preserves the reporter's raw traceback rather than assigning the defect to a particular subsystem.

solution.intent: Temporarily force specialize_int_float=True inside Dynamo's dynamic-shape context to bypass the SymInt dimension error.
solution.concrete_example: Change enable_dynamic() to use config.patch(dynamic_shapes=True, specialize_int_float=True), apply it together with PR 93059, and rerun training.

edges.comment: Actual failed workaround: after testing rather than merely planning to test it, the reporter reached compiled backward but then hit the int/_has_symbolic_sizes_strides exception.

question_patterns: Can you retest the original NeighborLoader benchmark on current PyTorch, Triton, PyG, and pyg-lib?
Does current Inductor now complete the dynamic training loop, and what are the eager and compiled epoch times?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Using the latest PyTorch, Triton, PyG, and pyg-lib, Inductor now runs through the benchmark. Eager averages 0.828314 seconds per epoch and compiled averages 1.081201 seconds. It prints 'Could not do split reduction due to dynamic shapes; performance may be worse.'

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The latest stack still fails during backward with the same int/_has_symbolic_sizes_strides exception.
The latest stack completes with nearly identical timings, but the warning is emitted from another dynamic reduction.

edges.comment: Version-update benchmark requested after several related compiler fixes landed. The user reports timings and the warning only; the performance interpretation remains engineer-side.

solution.intent: Use a current PyTorch/Triton/PyG stack with torch.compile(..., dynamic=True) for NeighborLoader training, retain the upstream dynamic-shape fixes rather than the failed local specialization hacks, and validate performance with synchronized, warmed-up end-to-end measurements.
solution.concrete_example: Update the source stack, compile the GCN with dynamic=True, warm up compilation, and time complete training iterations with CUDA synchronization. On the reporter's NeighborLoader script this ultimately completed and produced about a 20% speedup; separate basic-GNN measurements showed that apparent larger gains could change when synchronization and benchmark boundaries were corrected.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied raw exceptions, warnings, and timings. Engineers connected those observations to multiple compiler limitations: symbolic integer handling and insufficient guards in compiled backward, overspecialization, dynamic split-reduction limitations, PyG graph breaks, and CPU-side overhead. Engineers also identified that CUDA synchronization placement changed the apparent basic-GNN speedup. Those conclusions are inference, not facts originally stated by the reporter.

edges.comment: Reshaped (rule 4d): the fix is proposed here on pre-fix evidence; verification moves terminal-side.

question_patterns: Please re-run your NeighborLoader benchmark on the current nightly and tell me what you measure.
After updating, could you repeat the benchmark and report the numbers?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tested torch.compile with PyG again using my NeighborLoader GCN script, and I now get about a 20% speedup with the Triton backend.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The current build still crashes on changing NeighborLoader batches, so I cannot obtain a compiled timing.
The same script completes with an 18% rather than 20% speedup.

edges.comment: Post-fix verification (neutral patterns; the fix is not named to the user).

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the technical cause as incomplete dynamic-shape support across Dynamo, AOTAutograd, and Inductor for changing NeighborLoader batches, including symbolic-integer/guard handling and dynamic reduction limitations, rather than treating the GNN itself as invalid.

Diagnosis must be grounded in the observed progression: size/stride recompilations, the SymInt size() failure, the compiled-backward integer failure, the dynamic split-reduction warning, and the later successful run.
Must not recommend PR 93059 on the old Triton stack or the specialize_int_float=True eval_frame hack as the final fix; both were tried in-case and failed.

The final recommendation must use a current PyTorch/Triton/PyG stack with dynamic compilation and must benchmark after warmup with correct CUDA synchronization rather than relying on misleading asynchronous timing.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced PyTorch Geometric practitioner and container maintainer. Comfortable building PyTorch and Triton from source, applying small patches, updating benchmark scripts, and pasting full compiler tracebacks, but relies on compiler engineers to interpret Dynamo and Inductor internals.
persona_hint.communication_style: Persistent, concise, and cooperative. Shares exact commands, versions, timings, and tracebacks; asks direct questions about fixes and expected timelines; corrects earlier statements when a suggested patch had not yet actually been tested.
